page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.24xlarge is a storage-optimized Gen7 server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by a dedicated 48-core, 96-vCPU Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz, it incorporates 320 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware acceleration for AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system includes 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, 60,000 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. The architecture contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier performance in multi-threaded computational and storage-intensive workloads. The instance achieved top-tier relative results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 548.31 GB/sec, PassMark CPU testing at 93,157.6, and static web serving throughput reaching 128.24 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET throughput placed in the strong category, with Redis benchmark performance reaching 109.38 million operations per second. Prompt processing for large language models shows strong performance, though token generation speeds remain average due to execution on CPU hardware.

The inclusion of 60 TB local NVMe SSD storage paired with 768 GB DDR5 RAM provides substantial hardware density for stateful applications without external block storage dependencies. A key architectural tradeoff is single-core CPU execution, which sits in the middle tier under synthetic benchmarks, favoring parallel workloads over single-thread speed. The i7ie.24xlarge is suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, distributed cache layers, real-time analytics, and big data compression processing.
description: Amazon Web Services i7ie.24xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance running on the Nitro hypervisor. The server includes 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory and 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, alongside 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks highlight top-tier multi-threaded processing, achieving 548.31 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, a PassMark CPU score of 93,157.6, and static web serving throughput of 128.24 GB/sec. Database capabilities are supported by strong Redis performance reaching 109.38 million operations per second. While single-core performance tested in the middle tier, the high local storage density and memory bandwidth deliver qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale data tiers. The instance fits high-capacity database systems, in-memory caching, real-time telemetry analytics, and data pipeline processing.
